fields.name: coverageBand
fields.tooltip: Beam length as a fraction of the lane width (min, max), rolled per gate. Small on purpose: a gate is steered round, never jumped.

fields.name: beamRadius
fields.tooltip: Half thickness of the beam that burns, metres. The ship's own half width and half height are added on.

fields.name: beamHeight
fields.tooltip: Height of a horizontal beam's axis above the flight line, metres. 0 = dead on the ship.

fields.name: horizontalWeight
fields.tooltip: Relative weight of the single horizontal beam. 0 = never.

fields.name: verticalWeight
fields.tooltip: Relative weight of the single vertical beam. 0 = never.

fields.name: tripleWeight
fields.tooltip: Relative weight of three horizontal beams one above another. 0 = never.

fields.name: rotorWeight
fields.tooltip: Relative weight of the flat rotor. 0 = never.

fields.name: tripleSpacing
fields.tooltip: Triple: metres between one beam and the one above it. The upper two catch a ship in the air.

fields.name: verticalHeight
fields.tooltip: Vertical (procedural look only): how far above the flight line the beam reaches, metres. It starts at the road. A gate drawing the prefab is as tall as its sheet instead.

fields.name: rotorSpeedBand
fields.tooltip: Rotor: turn rate (min, max), degrees per second, rolled per gate; the direction is a coin toss.

fields.name: emitterScale
fields.tooltip: Scale of the emitter models. They are authored about 1.2 m across, which is a speck on a 100 m road.

fields.name: emitterSpinDegPerSec
fields.tooltip: How fast the emitters roll about their barrel (their local Z) while firing, degrees per second. B rolls the other way.

fields.name: emitterRoadClearance
fields.tooltip: Gap kept between the visible road and the lowest point an emitter can reach as it spins. A horizontal, triple or rotor gate is DRAWN lifted by whatever this takes (the burn stays on the flight line, where the ship's hit box is — the ship's model rides that much above it anyway); a vertical beam rises out of the road with its bottom emitter hidden.

fields.name: look
fields.tooltip: What draws the beam. Prefab = the laser model authored in PF_LaserSystem (its emitter bar and the beam sheet it projects down), at its authored size; Procedural = the old LaserA / LaserB emitters and code-built lines; Both = the two together. Prefab and Both make EVERY gate vertical (the variant weights are ignored) as tall as the sheet and burning as wide as it is; under Prefab alone no gate waves (the sheet cannot zigzag). A prefab with no authored model falls back to Procedural.

fields.name: prefabModelScale
fields.tooltip: Multiplier on the prefab's authored laser model, bar and sheet alike — never stretched. 1 = exactly as authored in PF_LaserSystem. The gate's height and burn width follow the sheet at this scale.

fields.name: beamMaterial
fields.tooltip: Additive material of the beam (URP Particles/Unlit, vertex colour). Empty = one is built in code.

fields.name: beamColor
fields.tooltip: Colour of the wide outer glow.

fields.name: coreColor
fields.tooltip: Colour of the thin hot core.

fields.name: glowWidthFactor
fields.tooltip: Drawn width of the glow as a multiple of the burning thickness (the core is a third of it).

fields.name: flickerAmount
fields.tooltip: How much the beam's width flickers, as a fraction of itself.

fields.name: flickerFrequency
fields.tooltip: Flickers per second.

fields.name: wavy
fields.tooltip: Beams may zigzag: a TRIANGLE wave (a sine's rhythm with sharp corners) running along the beam. The wave swings along the track's up — across the track on the vertical gate — and what burns grows by the amplitude on that axis, so the picture never lies.

fields.name: waveChance
fields.tooltip: Share of the gates that get the wave. 1 = every gate.

fields.name: waveAmplitude
fields.tooltip: How far the zigzag swings either side of the beam's axis, metres.

fields.name: waveLength
fields.tooltip: Length of one full zig + zag along the beam, metres.

fields.name: waveSpeed
fields.tooltip: How fast the wave runs from A to B, wavelengths per second. Negative runs it back; 0 = a frozen zigzag.

fields.name: waveTaper
fields.tooltip: Stretch at each muzzle over which the swing grows from nothing, metres, so the beam still leaves and enters the shoot points.

fields.name: activation
fields.tooltip: Gates start OFF: the sheet is pulled up into the bar and lets itself down onto the road as the ship closes in, sparks where it meets the road, and pulls back up once the ship is past. Only what is drawn burns. The authored (Prefab) look only. Off = every gate stands on from the moment it is built.

fields.name: growBand
fields.tooltip: Distance from the ship to the gate (full, start), metres: the sheet starts down at the far end and is on the road at the near one. Distances, not seconds, so it looks the same at any speed — keep the start inside the track reveal's seated edge (TrackReveal_Settings startAhead − band − stagger, ~866 m as shipped), or the sheet lets itself down while the gate is still collapsed and it rises in already on; keep the full end far enough out to steer round.

fields.name: passMargin
fields.tooltip: How far the ship must be past the gate before it pulls the sheet back up, metres.

fields.name: retractSeconds
fields.tooltip: Seconds the sheet takes to pull back into the bar once the ship is past (scaled time).

fields.name: floorContactThreshold
fields.tooltip: Share of its length the sheet must hang out before it counts as touching the road (the impact burst and the floor sparks). The sparks' look is the PF_LaserFloorSparks prefab nested in the laser prefab — tune it there.

fields.name: underTrackOverflow
fields.tooltip: How much further the sheet keeps growing past the road, down under the track, metres. 0 = it stops on the road. The grow band covers the whole length (sheet + overflow), so with overflow the sheet meets the road a little before the band's near end and keeps pushing down under it. Only the part above the road burns; the floor sparks still fire at road level.
